27 A stationary wave on a stretched string is set up between two points P and T.
S
Q
P
T
R
vibrator
Which statement about the stationary wave is correct?
A
Point R is at a node.
B
Points Q and S vibrate in phase.
C
The distance between P and T is three wavelengths.
D
The wave transfers energy from P to T.

hints: Notice where Q, R and S sit on the solid curve - at crests or a trough with large amplitude - and where the solid and dashed curves cross with zero displacement.
Recall that all points between two adjacent nodes form one loop and vibrate in phase, but adjacent loops vibrate in antiphase.
Count how many half-wavelength loops fit between P and T, then check how many loops separate Q from S to compare their phase.
walkthrough: Identify the pattern: the solid and dashed lines show the two extreme positions. Where they cross the amplitude is always zero, giving the nodes. P and T are nodes at the ends.
Count the loops between nodes. There is a Q crest loop, an R trough loop and an S crest loop, so there are 3 loops between P and T.
Use $\text{loop length} = \frac{\lambda}{2}$. So $PT = 3 \times \frac{\lambda}{2} = 1.5\lambda$, which rules out three wavelengths.
State the phase rule for a stationary wave: points in the same loop are in phase, points in neighbouring loops are in antiphase by $180^{\circ}$.

Apply it: Q is in loop 1, R is in loop 2, S is in loop 3. Q and the middle loop are in antiphase, and the middle loop and S are in antiphase, so Q and S are in phase with each other. This is option B.

A.explanation: Point R is at maximum displacement in the solid curve, so it is an antinode, not a node where amplitude is zero.

B.explanation: Q and S are antinodes in the first and third loops, separated by one whole loop, so they reach maximum displacement on the same side together.

C.explanation: P to T contains three loops, and each loop is $\frac{\lambda}{2}$, so PT is $1.5\lambda$, not $3\lambda$.

D.explanation: A stationary wave is formed by two opposite progressive waves and has no net transfer of energy along the string.
